comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
## 4K asset requirements (2026-08-30)

The rendering pipeline now scales UI/input natively and composes the map at display density. Bundled FOSS terrain remains at 128x64 through the normal-zoom 4K pipeline instead of being reduced to 64x32 first.

The original-size assets listed in this issue are now the remaining visual bottleneck. New FOSS replacements should target these minimum working sizes:

- full map tiles and full-tile overlays: 128x64 with alpha
- coast/dither quarter overlays: 64x32 with alpha
- compact UI icons: at least 2x their current logical dimensions
- city/unit/map sprites: at least 2x their intended 1920x1080 logical footprint, preferably larger source masters
- full-screen/advisor art: 3840x2160 or scalable/vector source

Keep source/master files when licensing permits, record author/license metadata, and do not derive or trace replacements from MicroProse assets. Runtime integration should retain the original Civ II logical footprint while sampling the higher-resolution source.

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
Partial progress landed in the standalone parity pass (`docs/CIV2-PARITY-AUDIT.md`, "Combat and unit abilities"):

- **Air fuel exhaustion** is now enforced at turn boundaries — `Game.Actions.ResolveAirFuel` counts consecutive turns a fuel-ranged air unit is away from a city/airbase/carrier and destroys it when the range is used up. (`MovementFunctions.cs:274` still carries a redundant inline `// TODO` at the per-move check point.)
- **Ships that must stay near land** — triremes now risk loss at sea with the documented 1-in-2 / 1-in-4 (Seafaring) / 1-in-8 (Navigation) odds, nil under the Lighthouse.

Still open for this issue: replacing the silent movement-error paths with player feedback, and the fighter-scramble / SAM battery / coastal-fortress combat messages.

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
Adding a data point from the Civilopedia-parity pass (`8ce5b47c`): **`MovementBlockedEventArgs` is raised but nothing consumes it.**

`LocalPlayer.MoveBlocked` fires `OnUnitEvent` with a `MovementBlockedEventArgs`, and grepping the UI finds no handler for that type — so every blocked move is silent today: zone of control, zero attack strength, cannot attack air units, edge of map.

That pass added a fifth reason, `BlockedReason.NotAmphibious`, for the new rule that only Marines may attack straight off a transport. The rule is enforced correctly, but a player who tries it with a Legion just sees nothing happen, which is a bad way to learn a rule the Civilopedia now states. Worth doing as part of the combat/movement feedback work here.

entries.title: Verify Civ II research-choice culling and key-civilization science costs
entries.author: crhy
entries.body:
Research selection and cost scaling are not yet fully faithful to Civ II. Difficulty-based choice culling is explicitly unfinished, and science cost currently uses PowerRank as though it were a civilization index when looking up the key civilization.

Source:
- Engine/src/AdvanceFunctions.cs
- Engine/src/Statistics/Power.cs

Acceptance criteria:
- Reproduce the number and culling of offered technologies by difficulty.
- Identify the key civilization from power rank without conflating rank with civilization ID.
- Verify cost modifiers for difficulty, tech paradigm, human/AI status, acquired technologies, and future technologies.
- Cover ties and eliminated civilizations.
- Add table-driven tests based on observed Civ II research screens.

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
Confirmed still unfixed on `master`:

- `AdvanceFunctions.cs:190` — `var keyCivAdvances = TotalAdvances(game, civ.PowerRank);` passes `PowerRank` straight into `AllCivilizations[...]` inside `TotalAdvances`, i.e. rank is still being used as a civilization index.
- `AdvanceFunctions.cs:230` — `CalculateAvailableResearch` still ends with `//TODO: cull list based on difficulty`; the full advance list is always offered.

comments.author: crhy
comments.body: Third item for this issue, found in the deep-audit pass: **every advance in `RULES.txt @CIVILIZE` is written with AI value `4`** (the 88 lines are all `Name, 4, 0, ...`). Civ II varies AI research value 2-6 per advance to steer the AI toward key military/economic techs; with every value equal, the AI's "pick the highest-value tech" logic has nothing to sort on and research order is effectively arbitrary within an epoch. This compounds T1 (the PowerRank-as-civ-id key-civ lookup) and T2 (no difficulty culling) already noted here.

entries.author: crhy
entries.body: And they're way too happy.

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
A few things that plausibly contributed have since been fixed on `master`:

- The bundled `@ENDWONDER` block was 28 lines of `nil`, so **no wonder ever obsoleted** — including the happiness wonders (Hanging Gardens, Michelangelo's, Shakespeare's, J.S. Bach's, etc.). Once built they made cities permanently content. The block now carries Civ II's obsoleting advances.
- `FindActiveWonder` now tolerates a city with no owner, fixing a crash in `GetFoodStorage` for freshly-founded cities.
- `CITY.txt` parsed as one 714-entry list, so every non-American civ threw `KeyNotFoundException` on founding its first city (fixed).

The growth path itself looks correct — `GameTurn.CitiesTurn` grows a city when `FoodInStorage >= (Size + 1) * RowsFoodBox`. Could you retest on latest `master` (plus PR #22, which fixes a hard crash on founding a city) and say whether cities still stall / stay over-content? If so a save or the turn number where it shows would help.

comments.body:
Fixed in `c3d3976e`.

`MovingPieces._holdTime` was `TimeSpan.FromMilliseconds(15)` — below the duration of an ordinary click, so nearly every map click registered as a Go To. Raised to 300ms, which makes it a deliberate press-and-hold.

entries.title: No lose state.
entries.author: crhy
entries.body: barbarians killed my first two settlers, then the game kept going without me.  LOL

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
There is no defeat path for the human. `Game.ChooseNextCivilizationOnce` (`Game.Actions.cs:88`) just `continue`s past a civ whose `Alive` is false — the `!Options.DontRestartIfEliminated` branch right below it is an empty `//Look to restart if possible` comment. Nothing sets `Alive = false` when a civ loses its last city and unit, and nothing raises a game-over for the local player. So losing every unit/city silently hands the turn to the AIs and the game continues.

Needs: (1) mark a civ eliminated when it holds no cities and no units (with the "settler in transit" grace Civ II gives on turn 1), (2) a local-player game-over notification when that civ is the human. Overlaps the game-over notification bullet in #10.

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
Fixed in `c3d3976e`.

Added `Game.CheckElimination`, called at the top of each civilization's turn in `ChooseNextCivilizationOnce`: a civ holding no cities **and** no units is marked `Alive = false`. Turn 1 is exempt so a civ still placing its first settlers is never judged, and barbarians are exempt.

Added `IPlayer.CivilizationDestroyed()`; `LocalPlayer` shows a new `@CIVDESTROYED` dialog ("Your Civilization Has Fallen"), so losing your last settler now actually ends your game instead of silently handing the turn to the AIs.

Not covered here: the `!Options.DontRestartIfEliminated` restart path is still the empty comment it was, and there is no scoring/replay screen — that belongs with the game-over notification bullet in #10.

entries.title: Great Library & Darwin's Voyage, stone dialog chrome, city-founding crash fix
entries.author: crhy
entries.body:
Three pieces of work plus a dev-tool commit.

## Great Library and Darwin's Voyage (parity backlog item 3)
Both wonders were cosmetic. Now:
- **Great Library** — `Game.ResolveGreatLibrary` runs at the start of the owner's turn and grants every advance that at least two other non-barbarian civs already know, via the existing `GiveAdvance` path. Stops when Electricity obsoletes the wonder. The qualifying-advance set (`WonderFunctions.GreatLibraryAdvances`) is unit-tested.
- **Darwin's Voyage** — `GameTurn.GrantWonderCompletionAdvances` grants two advances once, at construction, from `CalculateAvailableResearch` (highest AI value first).
- `CIV2-PARITY-AUDIT.md` updated.

## Stone dialog / side-panel chrome
`ImageUtils.SetLook` now cuts the MGE-style dialog and status-panel wallpaper from the painted `stonetexture.png` sheet (previously unused): brightness-matched limestone interior crops that keep text contrast, a darkened stone frame under the existing bevel. Falls back to the old flat fill when the sheet is absent. Also removes the black-checkerboard status panel seen in #18.

## Fix hard crash when founding a city — Fixes #24
`TextFileParser` treated any `@`-prefixed line as a new section, so the `@title=`/`@width=`/`@button=` property lines of standalone-only dialogs (`NAMECITY`, `FOUNDED`, …) were parsed as empty sections. `NAMECITY` got a null title and `CivDialog` dereferenced it — an NRE on every B press. Fixed the parser (a bare `@NAME` starts a section; `@key=value` is a property), stopped `Read.PopupBoxes` double-adding "OK", and added a null guard in `CivDialog`.

## F10 screenshot hotkey
Writes a PNG of the current frame (`RHYCIV_SHOT_DIR` or cwd). Used it to verify the stone work in the running client.

Quality gate: build clean, 173/173 tests.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

entries.title: MAINMENU dialog renders mostly off the right edge of the window
entries.author: crhy
entries.body:
### What happens

On launch (standalone / rhYciv Gold interface) the main menu dialog ("New game / Load map / Custom world / Load scenario / Load game" with radio buttons) renders with only its left ~quarter inside the window; the OK / Exit buttons are past the right edge and can't be clicked. The dialog also does not respond to Enter/Return, so from a fresh boot there is no visible way to start a game.

Observed at a 1600×900 window. Other wizard dialogs (e.g. CUSTOMCITY "City style") render fully on-screen and centred, so this is specific to MAINMENU.

### Leads

- `Civ2/Dialogs/MainMenu.cs:12` — `MainMenu() : base(Title, -0.08, -0.07)`. The other new-game dialogs pass no offset and are fine, so the negative-offset path in `CivDialog` positioning is the prime suspect (applied in the wrong direction, or truncated toward 0 as an `int` `Point` and then interacting with the width below).
- `CivDialog.cs:32` scales the declared width by `1.5` (`DefaultDialogWidth => 660 // 440*1.5`); combined with `DynamicSizingDialog` growing `_innerPanel.Width` to fit the radio-option labels, the dialog may end up wider than the offset math assumes.

### Also

MAINMENU (and the other `CivDialog` popups) ignore Enter as "activate default button" — worth confirming whether that's intended.

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
Fixed in `19bb5831` (branch `work/great-library-stone-ui`).

`MainMenu()` was passing a `(-0.08, -0.07)` position anchor, which `BaseDialog.SetLocation` interprets as "right edge 8% from the right, bottom edge 7% from the bottom". Once the inner panel grew to fit the radio labels the dialog overflowed the window from that corner and the OK/Exit buttons landed off-screen. Removed the anchor so MAINMENU centres like every other new-game wizard dialog; verified fully on-screen and clickable at 1600×900.

The Enter-as-default-button behaviour is a separate item and still applies — `CivDialog.OnKeyPress` only maps Enter when a button literally named `Labels.Ok` exists, and MAINMENU's confirm button is "OK". Worth a follow-up to map Enter to the first/confirm button generally.

entries.title: Founding a city hard-crashes (NRE) — standalone Game.txt dialogs parse with null titles
entries.author: crhy
entries.body:
### What happens

Pressing **B** to found a city throws `System.NullReferenceException` in `CivDialog..ctor` and takes the whole client down, every time.

### Root cause

`Civ2engine.TextFileParser.ParseFile` treats **any** line starting with `@` as the start of a new section. The bundled `RaylibUI/FOSSart/Standalone/Game.txt` writes dialog properties as `@title=`, `@width=`, `@button=` lines, so for a dialog defined only there — `NAMECITY`, `FOUNDED`, `ONLYSETTLERS`, `CITYATSEA`, `ADJACENTCITY`, `ONLY10`, … — every property line is parsed as its own empty section instead of a property of the dialog. `NAMECITY` ends up with `Title == null`, and `CivDialog`'s constructor calls `title.Contains(...)` with no guard.

`PopupBoxReader.ProcessSection` already has a switch for `width` / `title` / `button` / `options`, so it clearly expected those lines to arrive as content — the two components disagree. Dialogs that also have a `BuiltInDialogs` fallback (MAINMENU, DIFFICULTY, …) get a non-null title from there and so don't crash, which is why only the founding/other Game.txt-only popups blow up.

### Fix

Addressed in PR #22:
- `TextFileParser` — a bare `@NAME` starts a section; `@key=value` is a property line passed through as content.
- `Read.PopupBoxes` — stop appending a duplicate "OK" when the section declared its own `@button` lines (which now actually reach it).
- `CivDialog` — null-guard the title defensively.

Full test suite still passes (rules / labels / menu / events files use bare `@NAME` headers only).

entries.title: Combat resolution diverges from Civ II: per-round odds, terrain defence, wall/fortify stacking
entries.author: crhy
entries.body:
From the formula-level parity pass (`docs/CIV2-PARITY-DEEP-AUDIT.md`, section 1). Three distinct issues in combat math.

### 1. Per-round hit probability is not `A / (A + D)`  (major)
`MovementFunctions.cs:400`
```
probAttackerWins = defenseFactor >= attackFactor
    ? (attackFactor * 8 - 1) / (2 * defenseFactor * 8)
    : 1 - (defenseFactor * 8 + 1) / (2 * attackFactor * 8)
```
At A=D this is ~0.5, but at A2 vs D1 it returns ~0.72. Civ II rolls `rand(A+D)` each round and the attacker wins with probability exactly `A/(A+D)` = 0.67. The substitute over-rewards the stronger unit in every unequal fight.

### 2. `Tile.Defense` integer-divides away the ×1.5 / ×1.25 tiers  (major)
`Tile.cs:153` — `Defense => (River ? EffectiveTerrain.Defense + 1 : EffectiveTerrain.Defense) / 2` is `int`. Forest / Jungle / Swamp have rules-value 3 → `3/2 = 1`. A river on grassland → `(2+1)/2 = 1`. `DefenseFactor` multiplies by this truncated int, so wooded terrain gives no bonus and the river defence bonus is gone entirely. Should be `decimal`/`double` (`terrain.Defense / 2m`).

### 3. Fortress / Fortified / City Walls take `max()`, not the product  (major)
`UnitExtensions.cs:73-111` — `bestGroundFactor = max(fortress, fortified, walls)`, then `df += bestGroundFactor`. A fortified unit inside City Walls gets the walls term only; the ×1.5 for fortification is discarded. Civ II stacks these multiplicatively (Walls ×3 AND fortified ×1.5).

All three make defenders — especially in cities and forests — weaker than Civ II. Combined they favour the attacker substantially.

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
Fixed in `8ce5b47c` (v0.5.0-beta.1 line). All three, plus a fourth this issue didn't list.

**1. Per-round odds** — now `A / (A + D)`, the roll Civ II makes. The curve it replaced was symmetric at even odds but over-paid the favourite everywhere else (A2 vs D1 returned 0.72 instead of 0.67).

**2. Terrain defence** — `Tile.Defense` is a decimal multiplier instead of an integer division. The rules value counts half-steps, so Forest/Jungle/Swamp's 3 is ×1.5 again rather than ×1, and a river adds 25% the way Civ II applies it rather than being swallowed as another half-step.

**3. Wall/fortify stacking** — walls or fortress take the better of that pair, then fortification multiplies on top, rather than `max()` of all three.

**4. Not in this issue: City Walls added their effect value instead of multiplying by it.** `totalWallDefence = wallEffect / 100` was added to the defence rather than multiplied by it, so the shipped effect value of 200 gave every garrison a flat **+2** — a Phalanx behind walls defended at 4, not 6. This was arguably the biggest of the four and the deep audit missed it; the existing test even documented it with a `// That seems WRONG for City Walls` comment and asserted the wrong number.

Pikemen went the same way in the same pass (was ×1.5, and the mounted test required 1 HP so Dragoons and Cavalry — the units Pikemen exist to stop — were excluded).

Regression tests in `Core.Tests/Units/UnitExtensionsTests.cs`: walls multiply, walls stack with fortify, fortress stacks with fortify, Howitzer ignores walls, terrain half-steps as a theory over all four values, river +25%, and three Pikemen cases.

entries.title: Cities grow with no Aqueduct / Sewer System size cap
entries.author: crhy
entries.body:
`docs/CIV2-PARITY-DEEP-AUDIT.md` CG1.

`CityExtensions.cs:260` / `GameTurn.cs:62-66` — `GrowCity` is just `Size += 1`. `GameTurn.CitiesTurn` grows a city whenever `FoodInStorage >= (Size + 1) * RowsFoodBox` with no other check.

`ToExceedCitySizeAqueductNeeded` (8) and `SewerNeeded` (12) are parsed from `@COSMIC` into `CosmicRules` and exposed to Lua (`CosmicScripts.cs:216-223`), but no C# code reads them.

Civ II: a city stalls at size 8 without an Aqueduct and size 12 without a Sewer System. Also relevant: a city that loses its Aqueduct/Sewer while over the cap doesn't shrink but can't grow.

Partially referenced by #11 ("Link city growth limits to configured aqueduct and sewer improvements"); filing focused because it is a concrete, self-contained gameplay bug and a likely contributor to #13.

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
Fixed in `c3d3976e`.

Added `CityExtensions.CanGrow(rules)`, which reads the `@COSMIC` values that were already parsed but never used: a city cannot pass `ToExceedCitySizeAqueductNeeded` (8) without an Aqueduct, or `SewerNeeded` (12) without a Sewer System. `GameTurn.CitiesTurn` now consults it — when growth is blocked the food box is held full (the city does not shrink, matching Civ II) and the new `IPlayer.CityGrowthHalted` fires, which the local player shows as the `@FURTHERGROWTH` dialog.

A city that loses its Aqueduct/Sewer while already over the cap keeps its size and simply cannot grow, as in Civ II.

This may also be part of #13 — worth a retest of city growth on latest `master`.

entries.title: Production: no category-change penalty, no gold rush-buy
entries.author: crhy
entries.body:
`docs/CIV2-PARITY-DEEP-AUDIT.md` P1 / P2. Two Civ II production loops are absent.

### No production-change penalty
`ShieldPenaltyTypeChange` (50) is parsed from `@COSMIC` and used nowhere. `city.ItemInProduction = ...` is assigned directly in `GameTurn.cs:117`, `AiPlayer.cs:97,120` with no adjustment to `ShieldsProgress`. Civ II wipes ~half the accumulated shields (once) when you switch production between the unit / building / wonder categories; switching within a category is free.

### No gold rush-buy
No "hurry production" path anywhere in `Engine` or `RaylibUI` (grep for hurry/rush/buy is empty). Civ II lets you complete production with gold at an incremental cost — roughly `2*remaining + remaining^2/20` for a partially-built item, `4*remaining + ...` for a unit from an empty box, and a flat higher rate for wonders. AI also uses this.

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
Not fixed — worth flagging why, since it's less mechanical than it looks.

**Category-change penalty.** `city.ItemInProduction` is assigned in four places (`GameTurn.cs:120` auto-replace when an item becomes unavailable, `AiPlayer.cs:97,120`, plus the city window for the human) and also by both save-loaders. Hanging the penalty off the property setter would corrupt every loaded game, so it needs:
1. an explicit `city.ChangeProduction(item, rules)` used only at genuine change sites (not deserialisation, and arguably not the auto-replace path);
2. a `ProductionPenaltyApplied` flag on `City`, reset each turn — Civ II charges the 50% (`ShieldPenaltyTypeChange`) **once** per turn, and switching within a category is free, so the category of the item at turn start has to be remembered;
3. `City` gains a persisted field, so `JsonCityData` and the classic `.sav` reader both need the extra column.

**Gold rush-buy** is a feature rather than a fix: a cost formula, a treasury deduction, a City-window button, and an AI policy for when to spend. Nothing in `Engine` or `RaylibUI` has a hurry/rush path today.

Happy to take either on as its own piece of work — the first is maybe an hour, the second a good deal more.

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
Both halves done, shipped in v0.7.0-beta.1.

**Rush-buy** (`8f3b35e2`) — the Buy button had no click handler. It charges `2R + R²/20`, doubled for a wonder, doubled again when nothing has been put toward the item, and re-checks price and treasury before committing.

**Category-change penalty** (`20bee0af`) — this turned out to half-exist in the city screen, and to be wrong three ways:
- it split on `ItemType` alone, and wonders are Buildings, so switching from a building to a **wonder** counted as staying in category and cost nothing;
- it hard-coded a half instead of reading `ShieldPenaltyTypeChange`, exactly as this issue said was parsed and unused;
- there was no once-a-turn guard, so changing your mind twice was charged twice.

It is one engine call now — `City.ChangeProduction` — which the AI goes through as well, with tests for crossing categories, staying within one, the once-a-turn rule, and the rate coming from the ruleset.

While in there: the construction queue was still multiplying remaining cost by the shield box's rows, the last of the ten-times-price arithmetic from #41.

entries.title: Several city improvements have no effect or the wrong effect
entries.author: crhy
entries.body:
`docs/CIV2-PARITY-DEEP-AUDIT.md` TR1 / TR2 / TR3.

### No effect at all (`improvements.lua`)
- **Recycling Center** — Civ II: industrial pollution / 3 (`IndustrialPollutionModifier` 3).
- **Police Station** — Civ II: reduces field/war unhappiness under Republic/Democracy (the happiness pass already reads `PoliceStat`, but the improvement never gets the effect).
- **Super Highways** — Civ II: +50% trade on tiles with roads.
- **Hydro Plant / Nuclear Plant** — have `ProductionMultiplier` but not the industrial-pollution halving Civ II gives them (`CalculatePollution`'s own comment says "Modifier = 2 if city has Hydro Plant or Nuclear Plant").

### Wrong effect
- **Supermarket** — modelled as `Food +1 on irrigated tiles`; Civ II is +50% food from **farmland**, and farmland itself should require Supermarket + Refrigeration.
- **Manufacturing Plant** — `ProductionMultiplier` +25; Civ II is +50%.
- The four power plants are +25% each and **stack** with no Factory prerequisite; Civ II allows one per city, gated behind a Factory. (Already noted in the wonders/economy parity audit.)

### Pollution tech modifiers (`advances.lua`)
- Industrialization adds +2 to the population-pollution modifier; Civ II is +1.
- Sanitation is given -1 population pollution, which is not a Civ II effect.

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
Partly fixed in `c3d3976e` (the data-only ones):

- **Manufacturing Plant** — `ProductionMultiplier` 25 → **50**.
- **Recycling Center** — now has `IndustrialPollutionModifier 2`, which `CalculatePollution` turns into a divisor of 3 (`modifier = 1 + sum`). Previously it had no effect at all.
- **Hydro Plant / Nuclear Plant** — each gains `IndustrialPollutionModifier 1` → divisor 2, the halving Civ II gives them.
- **Industrialization** — population-pollution modifier +2 → **+1**.
- **Sanitation** — the non-Civ II `-1` population pollution effect removed.

Still open, because each needs engine support rather than a data value:

- **Super Highways** (+50% trade on road tiles) — there is no tile-trade effect in the `Effects` enum; `TaxMultiplier`/`LuxMultiplier` are city-level. Needs a new effect plus a hook in the tile-yield path.
- **Supermarket** — currently `Food +1 on irrigated tiles`; Civ II is +50% food from **farmland**, and farmland should require Supermarket + Refrigeration.
- **Police Station** — the happiness pass reads `PoliceStat` but the improvement never grants it under Republic/Democracy.
- **Power plants** — the four still stack at +25% each with no Factory prerequisite; Civ II allows one per city, gated behind a Factory.

entries.title: Government constants: Fundamentalism corruption-free, tax/lux/science caps mostly wrong
entries.author: crhy
entries.body:
`docs/CIV2-PARITY-DEEP-AUDIT.md` CE2 / CE5.

### Fundamentalism has zero corruption and waste
`RulesParser.cs:302-314` — `DefaultDistanceFromIndex` returns 0 for both Democracy (idx 6) **and Fundamentalism (idx 4)**, and `ComputeDistanceFactor` short-circuits distance 0 to no corruption / no waste. Civ II Fundamentalism has corruption on the order of Monarchy. (Communism at distance 0 is defensible — Civ II Communism does eliminate corruption.)

### Rate caps
`RulesParser.cs:282-300` `BuildTaxRateLimits`:

| Government | rhYciv | Civ II |
|---|--:|--:|
| Anarchy / Despotism | 60% | 60% ✓ |
| Monarchy | 80% | 70% |
| Communism | 70% | 80% |
| Fundamentalism | 80% (50% sci) | 60% |
| Republic | 80% | 80% ✓ |
| Democracy | 100% | 90% |

`RaylibUI/RunGame/GameControls/TaxRateWindow.cs:42` has its own hardcoded cap table — keep the two in sync when fixing.

Also minor (G2): Republic gets `NumberOfFreeUnitsPerCity = 0`; Civ II Republic supports a small number of units free per city.

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
Fixed in `c3d3976e`.

- `RulesParser.DefaultDistanceFromIndex` no longer returns 0 for Fundamentalism (idx 4), so it gets ordinary distance-based corruption and waste instead of Democracy's exemption. Communism keeps `CommunismEquivalentPalaceDistance` (Civ II really does zero its distance corruption) and Democracy keeps 0.
- `BuildTaxRateLimits` rewritten to the Civ II table: Anarchy/Despotism 60, Monarchy 70, Communism 80, Fundamentalism 60, Republic 80, Democracy 90. The separate 50% science cap for Fundamentalism is gone (Civ II caps all three rates equally and models Fundamentalism's science penalty as an output effect, not a rate cap).
- `TaxRateWindow._max` updated to the same table with a comment pointing at the parser, so the two stay in sync.

The Republic `NumberOfFreeUnitsPerCity = 0` point (G2) is untouched and still open — say the word and I'll fold it in.

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
Still not reproducible here, but there is now a crash log to work from — please retry on latest `master` and send me the file.

`e72b230f` makes the game write its own crash report. `Program.Main` catches unhandled exceptions from the loop, the AppDomain and the task scheduler, prints the stack to stderr, and writes it to a timestamped file under the per-user data folder (beside your saves — the bundled ruleset directory is read-only under Flatpak), naming the path on stderr. So a hard crash should now leave:

```
~/.var/app/io.github.crhy.rhYciv/data/AxxCiv/Logs/crash-<timestamp>.log
```

Reproduce, then attach whatever is newest in that directory.

**What I ruled out.** The harness now takes `RHYCIV_TEST_CITY=N` (a count, not a flag) and walks each settler clear of existing cities before founding, plus `RHYCIV_TEST_TURNS=N`. On seed 42: founding two cities, publishing both tiles, opening the second city's window and running four turns is clean. So the crash is not in `CityActions.BuildCity`, the city window, or the first few turns with two cities.

```
RHYCIV_AUTOSTART=1 RHYCIV_AUTOSTART_SEED=42 RHYCIV_TEST_CITY=3 RHYCIV_TEST_TURNS=4 dotnet RaylibUI.dll
```

**What I did not rule out**, because the harness calls the engine directly and skips it: the UI order path. `BuildCity.Update()` runs every frame and, when the active settler stands next to any city, builds an error dialog image — `Game.Players[city.OwnerId]`, `CityImages.Sets[cityStyleIndex][sizeIncrement]`. That branch is only reachable once a city exists, which fits "second city" precisely, and it would fire on moving the settler rather than on pressing B. If the crash happens as you *approach* your first city with the second settler rather than when you confirm the name, that is where I would look first.

Does it crash when you move next to the city, or only when you confirm the name in the dialog?

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
The crash logger paid off immediately — thanks for grabbing it. The stack named the line:

```
System.NullReferenceException
  at MovementFunctions.ExecuteUnitMove ... MovementFunctions.cs:755
  at MovementFunctions.Moveto ... :549
  at MovementFunctions.AttackAtTile ... :304
  at Game.ProcessBarbarianTurn ... Game.Actions.cs:480
  at Game.ChooseNextCivilizationOnce ... :105
  at EndTurn.Action() ...
```

Line 755 is `if (!game.ScenarioData.ForbidTechFromConquests)`, inside the city-capture branch. **`ScenarioData` was null in every new game** — `_scenarioData` was only ever assigned by the load-game constructor, never the new-game one. So the first time any city changed hands, by anyone, the game threw. Loaded saves were fine.

Fixed in `bbd3cb9a`: the field initialises to a plain `Scenario`, which is what a non-scenario game wants anyway — every restriction off.

**This is very likely what this issue has been all along.** Founding the second city spends the last settler, which leaves nobody awaiting orders, which is what triggers the first end of turn — and that is where the barbarians move for the first time. That also explains why it never reproduced by founding cities directly: my harness never reached an end of turn, and when I later made it run four, the barbarians happened not to take a city on seed 42.

Leaving this open until you confirm the second city is survivable now. If it still goes down, the new crash log will say where.

entries.author: crhy

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:

The engine **does** set a default: founding a city logs

```

```

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
Related root cause found and fixed in `e4769f28`, though it isn't the default-production part of this issue.

**Nothing could finish building at all.** `GameTurn` compared accumulated shields against `Cost * RowsShieldBox`, but `RULES.txt` costs are already shields — Warriors 10, Temple 40, Cure for Cancer 600, exactly Civ II's prices. So Warriors wanted **100** shields, and a young city making one a turn needed a hundred turns to raise one. Reported from play as "Warriors did not produce after 148 turns".

The same multiplication inflated the disband shield credit, the turn estimates in the Change-production list, and the size of the production shield box (a 10-shield unit drew a 100-slot grid).

Warriors now completes on turn 10 at one shield a turn, verified over a 12-turn headless run:

```
turn  2  Washington size 1 shields 1/10 producing Warriors (+1/turn)
...
turn 11  Washington size 2 shields 0/10 producing Warriors (+2/turn)  units 1 -> 2
```

Worth noting the interaction with civil disorder: a city in disorder `continue`s past production entirely, so a city stuck in disorder produces nothing. That was unfixable from the city screen until `bbd3cb9a` — see #28 and the entertainer work.

entries.title: Civilopedia promises the engine does not yet keep
entries.author: crhy
entries.body:
Now that `docs/CIVILOPEDIA-TEXT.md` is written and shipped (#39, #35), the Civilopedia is the player-facing specification: it states in plain words what every unit, building, terrain type and government does. That makes each remaining divergence a promise a player can read rather than an internal inconsistency.

The 2026-09-04 pass worked through the whole text and fixed everything cheap to fix (see #25 and `8ce5b47c`). This tracks what the text names that the engine still does not do. Full table with file references in `docs/CIV2-PARITY-AUDIT.md`, section "Civilopedia as the parity contract".

### Absent

- [ ] **Diplomat and Spy missions** — embassy, investigate, sabotage, steal tech, incite revolt, bribe. Backlog #5, issue #20. Largest single gap.
- [ ] **Caravan and Freight** — trade routes, deliver commodities, help build wonders. Backlog #6. Three unit entries describe this as their whole purpose.
- [ ] **Submarine stealth** — invisible to units that cannot spot it. Backlog #13. The flag parses and the movement restrictions work; visibility does not.
- [ ] **Nuclear strike** — area effect and fallout. Backlog #14.
- [ ] **Leonardo's Workshop** — upgrades obsolete units. Backlog #4.
- [ ] **Airlift** between cities with Airports. Backlog #11. Like Paradrop was, the Orders menu entry exists and is bound to no command.
- [ ] **Revolution and government change** — and Statue of Liberty with it. Backlog #15, #20. The seven government entries describe governments a player currently cannot switch between.
- [ ] **Marco Polo's Embassy, United Nations, Eiffel Tower** — all need diplomacy. Backlog #19.
- [ ] **Capitalization** — converts shields to gold. Issue #28.

### Already verified faithful

Checked in the same pass and needing no work: Fanatics' free support under Fundamentalism, the Trireme's must-stay-near-land loss chance, the Despotism/Anarchy penalty on any tile producing 3+, Fundamentalism's unhappiness suppression and half research and ten free units per city, Alpine Troops' road movement, the Howitzer ignoring walls, and AEGIS air defence.

### Note on wording

Every entry above hedges — each says the behaviour is "intended" — so no Civilopedia entry currently claims something the engine contradicts outright. They are promises not yet kept rather than statements that are false. Worth keeping that property: if an entry is rewritten to state a behaviour flatly, the engine needs to do it.

entries.title: Fix the coastlines
entries.author: crhy
entries.body: The need to be a tiny bit of beach close to the shore.  The current beach goes way out to sea.

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
Fixed in `e36c809b` — installed locally, not yet in a release.

You were right about the cause. The coastline tiles are painted from a signed distance to the shoreline, and **two** things in that ramp were wrong:

- The water did not reach deep ocean until **150 world pixels** out — half a tile — so every ocean tile touching land was bright turquoise edge to edge.
- Everything landward of the shoreline was painted sand, which is what put the beach half a tile out to sea.

The sea is now at full depth by about **57** pixels, and the sand is trimmed **46** pixels back toward the land. That leaves the thin bright shelf and narrow shore you get looking at a coast from above, which is the Civ IV read you described.

The marching-squares shoreline itself is untouched — running it through the middle of the tile is what keeps a coast smooth rather than stair-stepped, so that stays.

The move is applied to the distance just *before* the colour ramp, so every texture term after it — grain, foam, swell, caustics — still lands where it was tuned to. Nothing was repainted from scratch.

One note for whoever touches this next: `generate_coastline_iso.py` needs Pillow and numpy, which aren't on this machine, so `scripts/tune_coastline.py` performs the same move directly on the painted tiles by inverting the ramp per pixel. **The two carry the same two constants and have to be changed together.**

entries.title: Units display too small in the city window, and they're not quite where they should be in the boxes.
entries.author: crhy

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
Fixed in `45514aa5`, shipped in v0.7.1-beta.1 — two causes, one per half of the report.

**Too small:** the sprite scale was `ZoomScale(0) * 0.82f`, which evaluates to a flat **0.82 regardless of the city window's own scale**. The window defaults to 1.5, so the boxes grew and the units in them did not. The scale is now derived from the cell the unit is given — box size over rows and columns, against the unit rectangle — and multiplied by the window scale.

**Not quite where they should be:** `ListboxControlGroup` added every `UnitDisplay` at `(0, 0)`, so a sprite smaller than its cell sat up and to the left of where the box implied. They are centred in their cells now.

Both boxes go through the same helper, so Units Supported and Units Present stay consistent.

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
Fixed across e8a555b4 and 2ebdb4e3. Two separate faults:

**Placement.** The Units Present box shared its origin with the "Units Present" heading, so units drew over the label. The box moved below its heading, and Units Supported went to one row rather than two — the panel is 58 tall, so two rows gave each unit half the height of one in the box beside it.

**Size and sharpness.** The UI deliberately took the small classic sheet sprite while the map took the 1024px art. But `DrawScale`, `DrawOffset` and `LogicalSize` are all derived for the high-resolution art — `DrawScale` is roughly 48/1024 — so applying them to a sprite that was already the logical size drew it at a twentieth of its proper size, and blurry wherever it was scaled up. The UI now uses the same art the map does, so the metadata matches the texture it was measured against. This is also what made units tiny in the production box and the change-production list.

entries.title: Settler got stuck near a coast line and couldn't move.
entries.author: crhy
entries.body: I pressed K to automate and it started automating.

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
Fixed in e8a555b4. Three separate faults could each leave a unit unmovable and unselectable:

- **Automated settlers.** If the move an automated settler chose was refused — an enemy zone of control, or a settler with no attack strength meeting the unit standing in its way — the `Automate` order was restored anyway and no movement was spent, so it picked the same blocked square again every turn for the rest of the game. Automated units are not "awaiting orders", so it was never offered for selection either. A blocked automated settler now drops its order and comes back to you.
- **GoTo.** A unit blocked on the next square of its path was handed back to the player with the GoTo order still set, so it was not awaiting orders — and ending the turn came straight back into the same code and offered the same stuck unit again. The order is now cleared when the unit makes no progress.
- **Activation.** `SetUnitActive` switched the map into unit-moving mode even when the unit was refused (turn already ended), leaving the map pointing at a unit that wasn't there and nothing responding. It now falls back to the view piece.

Also, blocked moves were completely silent: the engine raised a `MovementBlocked` event and nothing in the UI listened to it, so a refused move was indistinguishable from a stuck unit. The reason is now reported (once per unit, per reason, per turn).

entries.title: Production Issue... Never produced warrior, Resources invisible in city window map.
entries.author: crhy
entries.body: This was on the second city, not the first.

comments.author: crhy
comments.body:
Partly reproduced, and I don't think it's one bug — leaving open.

I drove your exact setup headlessly (quick start, Deity, two cities, sixty end-turns) and got a city sitting at **+0 shields/turn, not in disorder, permanently stuck** — which matches "never produced warrior". Two things are going on and I want to separate them before claiming a fix:

**1. Unit support eats the shields.** Under Despotism free support is the city's *size*. The harness had built six units homed to a size-2 city, so four of them cost a shield each, against a gross of about four. Net zero, forever. That is Civ II-correct behaviour, but it is invisible: the city screen shows `Support: 4` and nothing explains why the shield box never moves.

**2. The cities were founded two tiles apart** and their work radii overlap heavily. The first city takes the good tiles, and `AutoAddDistributionWorkers` will only assign tiles with `WorkedBy == null`, so the second city ends up working little more than its centre. That would give both the low production **and** the "resources invisible in the city window map" half of this report — the resource overlays are drawn per worked tile, so a city working only its centre has almost none to draw.

So the question is whether what you saw was these two effects stacking, or a third thing. What would settle it: when you next hit it, open the second city and tell me what **Support** and **Production** read, and roughly how far apart the two cities are. If Support is large relative to the city size, it's (1). If the resource map shows terrain but no resource icons on the outer tiles, it's (2).

Separately, note that everything in your report predates the 10x production-cost fix landing in your build, so some of it may simply have been that.

One gap: **luxuries has no drawn art**, and it shares a row with taxes and science, so leaving it as the old sheet sprite would have put one coarse icon between two medallions. It is currently a violet-tinted copy of the gold medallion as a stand-in. A real luxuries badge would finish the set.

entries.title: Defork, cleanup, CI, and painted road/rail + city-window art (#67)
entries.author: crhy
entries.body:
Works through the [codebase review](https://github.com/crhy/rhYciv/issues/67) attached to #67, in the order that review suggested: identity debt first, then the build contract, then a correctness fix. Every commit leaves `scripts/quality_gate.sh` green (200 tests).

## 1. Defork

The product is rhYciv, but the solution, several project names, the engine namespace and the on-disk data directory still said Civ2-clone.

| Was | Is |
|---|---|
| `Civ2clone.sln` | `rhYciv.sln` |
| `Civ2/` | `UI.Classic/` |
| `Civ2Gold/` | `UI.Compact/` |
| `Civ2TOT/` | `UI.CompatAlternate/` |
| `Engine/Core.csproj` | `Engine/RhyCiv.Engine.csproj` |
| `Core.Tests/` | `RhyCiv.Tests/` |
| `namespace Civ2engine` | `RhyCiv.Engine` |
| `Engine/src/OriginalSaves` | `Engine/src/LegacySaves` |
| `Civ2Interface` / `Civ2GoldInterface` / `TestOfTimeInterface` | `ClassicInterface` / `CompactInterface` / `CompatAlternateInterface` |
| `Civ2WorldGenerator` | `ClassicWorldGenerator` |
| `Settings.Civ2Path` | `Settings.GameDataPath` |

Three of those are user-visible, so each keeps a back-compatible read path:

- **Save directory** moves from `AxxCiv/` to `rhYciv/`. `Settings.MigrateLegacyDataFolder` copies the old tree across once on first launch and leaves the original in place, so no save is lost and an older build still runs.
- **`Civ2Path` settings key** is still read when `GameDataPath` is absent.
- **Ruleset metadata key** written into saves becomes `"Compact"`; the loader maps the old `"Civ2Gold"` key onto it so existing saves resolve to the right interface instead of falling back to path matching.

Attribution in `LICENSE`, `NOTICE.md` and `ASSET-PROVENANCE.md` is untouched — it has to stay accurate. Comments describing Civilization 2 *mechanics* are also left alone; they document behaviour the engine deliberately reproduces.

Also removes real dead weight: `EtoFormsUI` left the tree some time ago but its build artifacts and a dangling project GUID in the solution's configuration section outlived it.

## 2. The build contract, in the build

`CONTRIBUTING.md` asked contributors to "target .NET 9 and preserve nullable annotations" and nothing enforced it.

- `Directory.Build.props` now owns `TargetFramework`, `LangVersion`, `Nullable`, `ImplicitUsings`, analyzers and deterministic/CI flags; the per-project copies are gone.
- **`TreatWarningsAsErrors` is on**, with `WarningsNotAsErrors` listing exactly the 18 rules the tree already violated (177 warnings, catalogued with counts in the file). It is a ratchet, not an exemption — no new warning class can appear, and codes come off the list as they are burned down. Verified by probe: `CS0162` (not listed) fails the build; the grandfathered warnings still pass.
- `Directory.Packages.props` centralises versions. Raylib-CSharp was declared independently in four projects; two Raylib versions in one process is a native crash with no useful stack. This also lifts `Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration` 5.0.0 → 9.0.0.
- `global.json` pins the SDK band.
- `.editorconfig` describes the style the tree already uses. `EnforceCodeStyleInBuild` is deliberately **off**, so it guides an IDE and `dotnet format` without failing builds on legacy formatting.
- `scripts/check_version_consistency.py` (wired into the quality gate) asserts `Directory.Build.props` and the Flatpak AppStream metainfo agree, so a tag can't ship a mismatched version.

Turning on `ImplicitUsings` brought `System.IO` into the engine, colliding with the engine's own `Units.Path`; three call sites now carry an explicit alias.

## 3. Interface discovery fails loudly

`LoadInterfaces` reflected over every DLL beside the executable and silently `continue`d past failures. An empty result surfaced later as an index exception from `interfaces[0]` — on a user's machine, with a stack trace pointing nowhere near the cause. It now reports what it scanned and what it skipped, and `GetInterface` guards its own precondition. The doc comment records that a trimmed or single-file publish would break here first.


## 4. Painted road and railroad connections

`docs/TEXTURE-GAP.md` listed the road/railroad rosettes as still generator-drawn vector. They now use the painted art from `~/rhYcivtextures`.

The renderer composites one sprite per connected neighbour (`Levels[level, neighbour + 1]`, falling back to `Levels[level, 0]` when isolated), so the art has to be **eight half-spokes plus a stub** -- each ending where that neighbour is actually reached: the midpoint of the shared edge for the four neighbours that share one, the diamond corner for the four that only touch at a corner. Two adjacent tiles each draw their half and they meet on the boundary.

`scripts/prepare_road_overlays.py` cuts the spokes from the straight-through source pieces: for each direction it picks the source best aligned with that axis, scales it to span exactly endpoint-to-endpoint on the diamond, and keeps the correct half with a small join overlap. Painted angles are used as-is and never rotated -- the art is already in 2:1 isometric screen space. Both sets resolved all 8 directions from 4 clean axis pieces each.

Two things needed a second pass: keying on colour distance alone left a pink halo (the painted edges are airbrushed, so a band of pixels is part matte), so the foreground is now eroded past that band and feathered back; and spokes are clipped to the tile diamond, because art outside it lands in the corners of the tile rect and visually overlaps neighbouring squares.

**This also fixes the procedural fallback it replaces.** `draw_connections` drew the full four-way rosette into *all nine* sprite slots, so a tile with one neighbour showed roads running off all four sides. It now draws one spoke per slot in the renderer's neighbour order.

## 5. Source-art audit

Every file in `~/rhYcivtextures` checked against what ships, recorded in `TEXTURE-GAP.md`. Two stale claims in that doc are corrected -- the cartographer background and the victory painting were both already wired. Still open: panel and city-window backgrounds are flat colour with a stripe every 26px while painted tileable stone sits unused; `main_menu.jpg` is generated and shipped but nothing reads it; `terrain/alts` holds seven unused paintings matching empty special-resource slots.


## 6. CI

The repository had no build or test workflow at all -- only a Flatpak job on tags. Nothing checked a pull request.

`ci.yml` runs `scripts/quality_gate.sh`, the same script the README tells contributors to run, across **ubuntu, windows and macos**. `ARCHITECTURE.md` documents save paths for all three, so all three are supported claims and should be tested claims. Both workflows now pin actions to commit SHAs rather than floating tags, cancel superseded PR runs (never master or tag builds), and declare `contents: read`.

It found two real bugs on its first runs, neither of which was reachable from a Linux dev box:

- `global.json` said `"version": "9.0.0"`, which is not valid alongside `rollForward` -- the SDK wants a full version including the feature band. The local dotnet tolerated it; `setup-dotnet` refused it on all three runners.
- **`ASSET-MANIFEST.tsv` failed to verify on Windows and only on Windows.** `assets()` sorted `Path` objects, and comparing `Path` objects uses the platform's own rules -- which are case-insensitive on Windows. `"Overlays"` sorts after `"ocean.jpg"` there and before it on Linux. Same files, same hashes, different row order, so the committed manifest read as stale. It now sorts on the POSIX relative path string, which depends on the paths and nothing else; the manifest is unchanged on Linux, which is what shows the fix is purely portability.

`.gitattributes` was added along the way, pinning the working tree to LF and marking binary asset types. That was my first reading of the same failure and it turned out not to be the cause -- but the manifest does hash five text assets (`RULES.txt`, `CITY.txt`, `Game.txt`, `describe.txt`, `pedia.txt`), and a CRLF checkout genuinely would break those hashes, so it stays as a closed hazard rather than a fix.

`quality_gate.sh` also resolves `python` the way it already resolved `dotnet`, which is what lets one script serve the whole matrix.

## 7. The city window

The window chrome, menu bar and side panels are all cut from the painted slate sheet, but the city window filled each of its own panels with a flat grey (84, 82, 78) that matched nothing else on screen -- the busiest screen in the game was the one that looked unfinished. This is the substance behind issues #64 and #65.

Neutral panels are now tiled with the same inner wallpaper the dialogs use. Food storage and production keep their flat green and blue: those are read as data, and a texture would fight the bars drawn over them. The texture comes from `TextureCache`, which owns the handle and drops it on a ruleset change.

Verified by running the game headless under Xvfb with the existing `RHYCIV_AUTOSTART` / `RHYCIV_TEST_CITY` / `RHYCIV_SHOT_DIR` harness and diffing captures. That is what caught the first attempt: leaving the panels unfilled to let the window background through looked right in principle, but the city window composites a classic backdrop the standalone set does not ship, and removing the fill put what lies underneath on screen. The fill has to stay opaque; only its material changes.

## Not in this PR

- **Detaching the GitHub fork link** needs GitHub Support; it cannot be done from the CLI. Worth filing, since it is the last piece of #67's identity section.
- **Renderer test coverage.** `RhyCiv.Tests` still only covers the engine. The review's suggestion to extract the pure zoom/tile maths into `RaylibUtils` and test it there remains the highest-value option.
- **Save schema versioning.** Saves do carry a `version` field (0.1), but there is no migration chain and no round-trip tests.
- **The remaining flat backgrounds.** `panel.jpg` still backs the seven advisor screens, and `city_land/river/ocean.jpg` still back the city view. Unlike the city window there is no painted source art for those, so they need art before they need code.
- **`main_menu.jpg`** is generated and shipped but nothing reads it.
- The **177 grandfathered warnings** are ratcheted, not fixed. Burning down `CS8602` and `CS8618` would cover three quarters of them.
